newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Lafontaine says ready for new tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Lafontaine says ready for new tax talks.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said late on Monday he was ready for new talks to try to reach agreement over planned tax reforms with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition.
"It is possible now for us to communicate informally, if the coalition could agree amongst themselves," Lafontaine told German ARD television.
Lafontaine said the main bone of contention between the SPD and the ruling coalition remained the government's plans to cut top 53 percent rate of income tax and benefit higher earners.
Earlier the SPD launched proposals to restructure some 78 billion marks of revenues in the tax system, giving tax breaks to families and workers while raising revenues elsewhere.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, while accusing Lafontaine of mere "crowd-pleasing" with the plan, insisted the government was nonetheless ready to restart talks with the SPD any time.
Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said he saw some positive aspects in the new SPD plan, saying they provided a good basis for quick agreement.

But Hermann Otto Solms, parliamentary leader of junior coalition partners the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) who are staunchly opposed to any tax hikes to help Bonn fill a gaping budget gap, said new talks were pointless, because the SPD's new plans were half-baked.
